lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Today we’re looking at how caffeine acts in the brain, and what it may mean for sleep and memory.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ribeiro and Sebastião say caffeine mainly works by blocking adenosine receptors, affecting brain functions including sleep, learning, and memory.
lines.quote: Caffeine causes most of its biological effects via antagonizing all types of adenosine receptors

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Landolt describes adenosine as a sleep-regulating substance, while noting open questions about how caffeine changes sleep.
lines.source: Adenosine, caffeine, and sleep–wake regulation: state of the science and perspectives
lines.quote: Today, adenosine is widely accepted as an endogenous sleepregulatory substance.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A review of sleep and daytime functioning also raises a trade-off: caffeine may affect nighttime rest and next-day performance.
lines.source: Effects of caffeine on sleep quality and daytime functioning
lines.quote: the relationship between caffeine consumption and subsequent quality and quantity of nighttime rest

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: On memory, the evidence is mixed. One review says there is no reliable long-term memory effect, with results varying by task.
lines.source: How does caffeine influence memory? Drug, experimental, and demographic factors
lines.quote: There is no reliable effect of caffeine on LTM

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That review notes a study where 200 milligrams after learning improved delayed recognition, but another study did not replicate it.
lines.source: How does caffeine influence memory? Drug, experimental, and demographic factors
lines.quote: Aust and Stahl (2020) failed to replicate the findings of this study

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The authors suggest withdrawal reversal may partly explain that earlier positive result.
lines.source: How does caffeine influence memory? Drug, experimental, and demographic factors
lines.quote: likely the reversal of withdrawal symptoms from caffeine abstinence escalated the positive treatment effect.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A face-recognition experiment found no consolidation benefit; instead, caffeine reduced recognition accuracy.
lines.source: Caffeine reduces accuracy in face recognition memory consolidation
lines.quote: caffeine consumption did not improve the consolidation of face recognition memory.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the findings differ: an earlier object-memory study reported improved discrimination, but face memory showed impairment.
lines.source: Caffeine reduces accuracy in face recognition memory consolidation
lines.quote: a general impairment in recognition performance

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The broader review suggests caffeine may influence memory indirectly through attention, mood, and alertness, rather than reliably strengthening memory itself.
lines.source: How does caffeine influence memory? Drug, experimental, and demographic factors
lines.quote: increasing attentional control and processing resources or modulating learning factors including mood, concentration, arousal, and alertness.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The one thing to remember is that caffeine can change alertness, but it is not a dependable memory enhancer.
lines.source: How does caffeine influence memory? Drug, experimental, and demographic factors
lines.quote: very limited treatment effects of caffeine on memory performance.
